newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha jumps on firm fundamentals.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha jumps on firm fundamentals.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices gained on Thursday on firm fundamentals in a market conspicuously lacking active sellers, traders said.
Traders said fundamentals appeared firm with buying interest keen. They said the market was very thin due to the absence of many traders due to the Chinese New Year.

Open-naphtha first-half April was notionally assessed at $241.00/243.00, up about three dollars from late Wednesday levels. Second-half April was some three dollars lower at $238.00/240.00, up from $235.00/236.00 late on Wednesday.
Backwardation in inter-month spreads has deepened.
Second-half March/second-half April was notionally assessed at $5.50/6.50. The level was the same for first-half April and first-half May.

"I think the physical market, particularly in the prompt, still looks quite strong," a trader said. He said there were some Japanese traders possibly looking for second-half April delivery but finding cargo availability scarce.
Market participants for both naphtha and gas oil said they believed Chinese participants might seek cargoes when they return to the market after the Chinese New Year holiday.
